chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Umar ibn Yazid, who said:
I said to Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: What do you say about i'tikaf in Baghdad in some of its mosques?

He said: "Do not perform i'tikaf except in a congregational mosque in which a just Imam has led the congregation in prayer. There is no harm in observing i'tikaf in the مسجد of Kufa, Basra, the مسجد of Medina, and the مسجد of Mecca."

key_terms.إِمَامٌ عَدْلٌ: a just Imam who leads prayer with upright legitimacy
key_terms.الِاعْتِكَافِ: spiritual retreat in the mosque devoted to worship
key_terms.الْكُوفَةِ: Kufa, one of the specifically mentioned mosques for i'tikaf
key_terms.الْمَدِينَةِ: Medina, one of the specifically mentioned mosques for i'tikaf
key_terms.مَسْجِدِ جَمَاعَةٍ: a congregational mosque where communal prayer is established

ai.seo_question: In which mosques is i'tikaf valid according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the validity of i'tikaf, restricting it to a congregational mosque in which a just Imam has led the prayer. It specifically permits i'tikaf in the mosques of Kufa, Basra, Medina, and Mecca, highlighting the jurisprudential conditions and recognized sacred spaces for this act of worship.
